dataset.description: The proposed project targets plasmepsin V for highly selective inhibitor design as it is the most structurally distinct enzyme from both Plasmodium and human aspartic proteases. Two approaches will be applied: (i) screening for non-peptidomimetic inhibitors targeting flap loop region and (ii) design of targeted covalent inhibitors to selectively bind unpaired cysteine in the flap loop region of PM V.  The proposed project seeks to develop novel covalent PM V inhibitors that might eventually lead to cost effective and selective antimalarial drugs. Computational and in vitro screening approaches is utilized to identify PM V inhibitors, with particular emphasis on selectivity against non-target proteases. The docking models is based on the available crystal structures of PM V (PDB ID: 4ZL4 and 6C4G) and are validated using known PM V inhibitors. Inhibitory potency of potential inhibitors is determined using a time-resolved fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay.

distribution.title: The data is collected to identify non-peptidomimetic plasmepsin V inhibitors as potential antimalarial leads. Data generated from organic synthesis, enzymatic assays, computational drug design, and structural studies will be systematically collected and documented. Research data, including structural data (e.g., Protein Data Bank (PDB) entries) and experimental results, will be shared through public repositories: Zenodo for general data, PDB for structural data, and GitHub for software or code produced during the project. Open-access publication will be prioritized for scientific outputs. The Data Management Plan (DMP) is designed to enhance research transparency, facilitate collaboration, and advance antimalarial drug discovery.
